newsitem.title: UK: N. Rock raises UK mortgage rates, sees base rise.
newsitem.headline: N. Rock raises UK mortgage rates, sees base rise.

text.p: Northern Rock Building Society said on Monday it would raise its mortgage rates from January 2 1997 and said it believed Chancellor Kenneth Clarke would raise interest rates by at least a further 1/4 point soon.

"Our new rates reflect our belief that the Chancellor will raise rates by at least a further 0.25 percent over the next month or so. We've delayed the increase until the New Year to allow us only to make one change instead of two," Northern Rock executive director Adam Applegarth said in a statement.
UK base lending rates were raised by 1/4 point to 6.0 percent on October 30.
Northern Rock's standard rate will rise to 7.49 percent, or 6.99 percent for borrowers who have held their current mortgage for more than seven years.
The rise follows a move at the weekend by Abbey National Plc, which said it was raising its mortgage rates by 1/4 point, and a rise by the Coventry earlier on Monday.
